rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 <U+2014> two-year replicated field experiment at Russell Ranch, three 0.4 ha blocks, SDI/DDI vs FI, organic processing tomato, yield from machine harvest and water from flow meter. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 1b <U+2014> SSD gave significant IWP gains over furrow in both years with no significant yield decrease despite 17% (2015) and 36% (2016) less irrigation water. Q4: Section 3.2, Fig. 2, Table 2 <U+2014> gravimetric water content measured at nine distance-depth positions; FI had higher moisture at 20-40 cm centre and throughout 40-60 cm, interpreted in Discussion as displacement by excess irrigation water in FI, i.e. the concentrated wetting zone/less lost water under SSD that underlies the IWP gain. Q8: Discussion <U+2014> authors restrict the result by noting that the IWP measured here is short-term crop per unit of applied water and overall system water-use efficiency must account for microbial and soil-structure changes; Conclusions note the study covers only the two years after SSD installation and provides preliminary evidence. Q9: Fig. 1 caption <U+2014> error bars indicate standard error for yield and IWP.
rows.notes: Q3 no: IWP derived from a single harvest-and-flow-meter method; hand harvests only confirmed machine harvest (same method). Q4 is a judgement call: soil moisture distribution was measured, but the IWP gain is largely arithmetic from the lower applied volume with equal yield. Q5/Q6 no: one site, one crop, plot scale (0.4 ha blocks). Q7 no: no stated requirement for the IWP gain; irrigation scheduling by ET0 sensor is described, not framed as a condition.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1 and 2.5 <U+2014> own field trial with weed counts in ten quadrats per treatment per block on one date each year. Q2: Section 3.3 and Fig. 3 <U+2014> SSD treatments had fewer than 0.15 weeds m-2 in both years; weed density higher in FI by a factor of 30 (2015) and 100 (2016), no difference between SDI and DDI.
rows.notes: Q3 no: weed density measured by quadrat counts only. Q4 no: the mechanism (reduced surface wetting prevents germination) is asserted in the Fig. 3 caption; although GWC was measured, surface 0-20 cm moisture did not differ significantly among treatments (Table 2), so the intermediate variable was not shown to link to the weed effect. Q5/Q6 no: single site, one crop, plot scale. Q7 no: no condition stated as required for weed suppression. Q8 no: no limitation stated for the weed result specifically (single counting date is reported in methods but not framed as a limitation). Q9 no: Fig. 3 reports letter groupings and ratios only; no SE, SD, CI or range given for weed density.

notes: Full text available; supplementary figures not included but not needed for the rated claims. Both claims are directly supported by the study's own results; the review passages closely paraphrase Sections 3.1 and 3.3.
